display.purpose: The one big word of a full screen («Подборка», «Cloudify», offline title); scales with its container, single line. «Библиотека» uses min(108px, 12.5cqi).

headline.purpose: Title of a section page that is not built yet.

lead.purpose: The single line under a display word; white at 80% with a soft shadow on the light.

title.purpose: Track and playlist titles in rows, cards and the player (14–16.5px).

label.purpose: Counts, durations, timestamps, helper text; tabular figures.

badge.purpose: State badges on track rows and the keyboard hint.

fitted-name.purpose: Opened playlist or person name, measured to fit: one line up to 112px while ≥64px, else two balanced lines up to 84px (≥44px), else three at 34–60px. Unbounded 800, 0.92, −0.055em.

shadows.name: floating-menu
shadows.purpose: Popovers over content, always with a line border.

shadows.name: hero-cover
shadows.purpose: The large cover in the hero and the opened playlist/person face beside its name.

shadows.name: inner-rim
shadows.purpose: Edge of smoky buttons, chips, the filter well on the light, and the rounds on a cover. Also the learning badge on the light.

shadows.name: play-round-over-cover
shadows.purpose: The 56px white play round on a track tile; the 44px round on playlist and station tiles uses 0 10px 24px -10px.

shadows.name: now-playing-ring
shadows.purpose: Ring around the playing track's cover on a wall or shelf.

shadows.name: text-on-light-display
shadows.purpose: text-shadow for the display word over the ribbon.

shadows.name: text-on-light-lead
shadows.purpose: text-shadow for the lead line over the ribbon.

shadows.name: sheet-up
shadows.purpose: The key help and «Настроить подборку», rising from the player bar's full width; the queue sheet uses floating-menu.

shadows.name: drag-ghost
shadows.purpose: The ghost of a queue row held by its grip, on panel-hover.

shadows.name: key-used
shadows.purpose: glow-1 underline of a drawn key that does something.

shadows.name: status-ping
shadows.purpose: The status button when an action fails: a fading glow-1 ring with a 1.08 scale, not a lift.

shadows.name: slider-knob
shadows.purpose: The 24px white knob of the desk's balance slider.

shadows.name: new-track-ring
shadows.purpose: A cover from the new side in the desk's strip (1.5px on its legend tag). A ring, not a lift.

motion.name: glow-crossfade
motion.purpose: Cover colours cross-fade on :root when the track changes; none under reduced motion.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Colour changes on hover and press for buttons, rows, panels, tabs.

motion.name: topbar-backing
motion.purpose: The top bar's backing and blur appearing once the page scrolls past 8px.

motion.name: press-spring
motion.purpose: White pills; the 44px player play button uses 1.05 / 0.95.

motion.name: ribbon-frame-rate
motion.purpose: The light redraws at about 30 / 15 fps, stops when hidden or off screen, never runs under reduced motion.

motion.name: mood-ease
motion.purpose: Energy and pace of the light ease toward a new mood instead of jumping.

motion.name: relight
motion.purpose: The library's light crossing to an opened item's or the playing cover's colours; none under reduced motion.

motion.name: relight-quick
motion.purpose: The light following the cover the pointer or focus rests on.

motion.name: tile-hover
motion.value: cover scale 1.04 over 300ms ease-out; veil, play round and corner rounds 150ms
motion.purpose: Track tile hover/focus anatomy; corner rounds rise 4px.

motion.name: sticky-backing
motion.purpose: The library actions row growing the top bar's backing once stuck.

motion.name: notice-timeout
motion.purpose: A player notice (and its one action) steps aside.

motion.name: ease-sheet
motion.purpose: Easing of the sheets over the player and of the queue's gap slide.

motion.name: sheet-rise
motion.purpose: The queue sheet rising out of the queue round; none under reduced motion.

motion.name: sheet-up
motion.purpose: The key help and «Настроить подборку» rising out of the player bar; none under reduced motion.

motion.name: gap-slide
motion.purpose: Queue rows sliding over by one row to open the gap for a dragged row.

motion.name: key-press
motion.purpose: A drawn key lighting, and dipping 1px at 96% when pressed.

motion.name: status-in
motion.purpose: The status button arriving when something goes wrong; none under reduced motion.

motion.name: status-ping
motion.value: 900ms ease-sheet; scale 1 → 1.08 → 1 with the status-ping ring
motion.purpose: The status button catching the eye when an action fails; none under reduced motion.

motion.name: drop-in
motion.purpose: «Что не так» and the «Вход устарел» sheet dropping from the top bar; none under reduced motion.

motion.name: light-out
motion.purpose: The light going grey while offline or signed out, and its colour coming back the same way; instant under reduced motion.

motion.name: network-back
motion.purpose: How long «Сеть вернулась» stays in the status button.

motion.name: offline-dot
motion.purpose: The grey dot of «Нет сети».

motion.name: strip-slide
motion.value: transform 160ms ease-sheet; new covers from opacity 0, scale(0.94)
motion.purpose: Covers in the desk's strip moving to their new places as the balance changes; still under reduced motion.

motion.name: knob-hold
motion.purpose: The balance slider's knob while dragged.

breakpoints.name: home-grid-two-columns
breakpoints.purpose: At and below: the home grid and «Настроить подборку» go to two columns (the desk's balance spans both, its strip 12 across).

breakpoints.name: player-compact
breakpoints.purpose: At and below: now-playing column 180px, volume slider 72px; key map in one column; while the selection plays, right-hand controls 6px apart, separator, lyrics and shuffle step out, the «почему» line and a notice wrap to two lines.

narrative.overview:
Cloudify is a near-black room with one light source: the cover of whatever is playing. Three hues are read from that artwork, lifted so they glow on a dark ground, and drawn as a soft ribbon of light behind one very large word. Everything else in the window stays neutral, so the music is always the only colour on screen. When the track changes, the whole interface (the light, the progress fills, the mark, the focus ring, the text selection) cross-fades to the new cover over 1.6 seconds.

The window is built for hours of background listening. The light swells with the playing track's real loudness curve, slows to a drift when paused, and costs almost nothing when nobody is looking. Type is big and heavy where it names a place and calm everywhere else. Surfaces are soft, rounded, tonal steps of near-black; actions are white pills and smoky rounds. Real artwork appears wherever a track, playlist or person is shown, and a missing cover is a quiet tile, never a broken image.

The mood is close to a large streaming service's dark "for you" screen in polish and energy, but the layout, names, mark and colours are Cloudify's own. No fixed brand accent exists, and none of SoundCloud's or Yandex Music's brand marks or signature colours are used.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground; all colour comes from the playing cover through three live `--glow-*` variables.
A blurred, grain-covered ribbon of light behind one huge Unbounded word.
White pill for the primary action; smoky round buttons with a 1 px inner rim for the rest.
Heavy Manrope (600 and up) for all running text; Unbounded only for names of places.
Rounded tonal panels instead of borders and shadows.
Big real covers as the way into music: a wall you point at, and the light takes the hues of what you point at.
Motion that is slow, soft, cheap at idle, and off under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Music Paints Rule
rules.body: No component gets a fixed accent colour. Anything that needs emphasis takes `glow-1`/`glow-2` (or white for actions); everything else stays on the neutral scale.

rules.name: The No Yellow Turn Rule
rules.body: Moods may rotate the cover's hues (`hueShift`), but a rotated hue that lands between 44° and 68° is pushed out to orange or lime. A cover's own yellow is the music's and stays; a yellow the app produces itself is never allowed.

rules.name: The Cross-Fade Rule
rules.body: Glow colours never jump. They are registered with `@property` and transition over 1.6 s on `:root`; reduced motion switches them instantly.

rules.name: The Pointed Light Rule
rules.body: A page's own light may borrow colours locally by setting `--glow-*` on its wrapper: first from the cover the pointer or focus rests on (a tile on a wall, or a found track's row), else from the opened playlist or person, else from the artist a search names, else it keeps the playing track's. Pointing answers the hand in 0.6 s after a 70 ms rest (so a sweep across covers does not flicker); everything else crosses over in 1.6 s; leaving the covers gives the light back. Only the light relights: progress fills, focus ring and selection keep the playing track's colours.

rules.name: The Smoke On Light Rule
rules.body: Anything placed on the light is smoke with a rim, never veil: a white wash vanishes into the light's brightest band. Veil is for wells on ground.

rules.name: The Grey Light Rule
rules.body: While there is no network or the sign-in has expired, the light from the cover goes grey (`grayscale(1) brightness(0.5)`) on the shell and on the sign-in and unreachable stages, and the colour comes back the same way when they return, both over 1.6 s (instantly under reduced motion). The ribbon keeps moving; only its colour is taken. Nothing else in the window changes colour for it.

rules.name: The Place Name Rule
rules.body: Unbounded names places: the hero word, page titles, section titles, the titles of panels and sheets («Клавиши», «Настроить подборку», «Что не так», «Вход устарел», «Сколько хранить», «Где ты»), the diary's day dates and the wordmark. It never sets a track title, a button, a label or a sentence.

rules.name: The Heavy Body Rule
rules.body: Manrope never drops below 600. Hierarchy among small text comes from weight (600 / 700 / 800) and the three text tones, not from thin weights.

rules.name: The Windowed Wall Rule
rules.body: A wall that can hold thousands of covers keeps only the rows near the screen in the page (two rows of overscan), all rows one fixed height, so 5 000 likes scroll and filter as lightly as one screen. Loading walls show quiet `panel` tiles in the wall's own rhythm.

rules.name: The One Row Shelf Rule
rules.body: A shelf shows one row that fits the window and nothing more; the rest is one click away through its title, never behind a sideways scroll.

rules.name: The Answer First Rule
rules.body: A search leads with what it most likely means. An artist becomes the page's hero (name, face, «Радио артиста») only when SoundCloud ranks a same-named account in its top three people and that account is verified or has 5 000+ followers; otherwise the query itself is the title and the tracks are the answer. While typing, a name that starts with what is typed (from three letters) will do. A namesake never takes the hero.

rules.name: The Every Name Opens Rule
rules.body: An artist's name or face, wherever it is shown (a tile, a row, the player, the home screen, a playlist's lead, the search hero), opens that artist's page: in place of the results while searching, else in the library. A name inside a row or card that plays sits above the row's own play target, so the rest of the row still plays.

rules.name: The Read First Rule
rules.body: Found tracks are rows, not covers: a found title is read before it is played, and re-uploads come with long, messy names that a caption under a cover cuts short. The wall of covers is for music you already know (the library).

rules.name: The Strip Keeps Three Weeks Rule
rules.body: The diary's day strip narrows its columns before it shows fewer than 21 days, so the last three weeks are always one glance; it never scrolls sideways.

rules.name: The Counted Choices Rule
rules.body: A filter offers what the results actually hold. The genre list is the search's own genres as SoundCloud counts them, each with its count, counted with the other filters but not the genre, so a choice never empties the list by surprise; a chosen genre stays listed even when the counts stop naming it. Totals on chips and titles are SoundCloud's estimates and are shown as such, never padded.

rules.name: The Tonal Step Rule
rules.body: Cards and tiles are flat panels; they never get a drop shadow. A shadow means the thing is floating over other content (a menu, a sheet over the player, a dragged row, a white play round over artwork) or is the hero cover and its twin, the opened face.

rules.name: The Grain Over Light Rule
rules.body: Any surface that shows the ribbon also carries the grain overlay.

rules.name: The Cheap Light Rule
rules.body: The ribbon redraws at about 30 fps while playing and 15 fps while paused, paints into a canvas a quarter of its drawn size (the light is all soft edges, so stretching it costs nothing visible), stops when it is off screen or the window is hidden, and does not animate at all under reduced motion. Mood changes ease in over roughly half a second.

rules.name: The Honest Queue Rule
rules.body: The queue never claims more than happened. The played-before tab is «Уже играло» only when every track above the playing one really played; when some were only passed over (a jump forward, a list started from its middle) it is «Выше в списке». The end of the list says how the queue will really end, with the key that changes it.

rules.name: The Quiet Keys Rule
rules.body: The window's single keys (space, arrows, digits, letters) stay silent while typing in a field, leave a focused control the keys it handles itself (a slider's arrows, a keyboard-focused button's space, a queue row's arrows), and never take Cmd or Ctrl shortcuts; the only ones the app uses are ⌘K / Ctrl+K and ⌘F / Ctrl+F, handled by the search and the filter. Held down, only seek and volume repeat. Esc closes the key help first, then the desk, then the queue, and leaves an open menu its own Escape.

rules.name: The Physical Keys Rule
rules.body: Hotkeys are read by the key's place on the keyboard, not the letter it types, so Q, S, R and M work the same in the Russian layout; the help draws them in Latin.

rules.name: The Worked-Out Reason Rule
rules.body: The «почему» line, the strip's reasons and the desk's counts quote only facts the engine worked out from the diary as it is now, and they are worked out again whenever the diary changes: an erased diary reads «пока по правилам — тебя ещё не выучил», never what it said before. The most telling part comes first («Дослушал 7 из 11 · из твоих лайков»), at most two parts, and its figures are held whole by no-break spaces so a narrow line never splits «7 из 11».

rules.name: The One Song Rule
rules.body: One song is one identity across its uploads: a version or re-upload plays once in the selection, and a re-upload of a song you liked or just played is never offered as new.

rules.name: The Honest Source Rule
rules.body: A source with nothing to give says why and when it will fill («Пусто: появится в октябре 2027, когда дневнику будет год»), in muted text where a full source's line is faint; its weight group stays hidden until there is something to weigh.

rules.name: The Rules By Default Rule
rules.body: Before the diary holds a play the selection says it plays by default rules («Правила по умолчанию»; «Пока по правилам: два лайка, потом трек со станции» as «Как обычно»'s lead), while learning it says how far («Учусь: N из 30»), once learned how much it learned from («Подбираю по твоему дневнику — N прослушиваний»). It never claims to know you before it does.

rules.name: The One Place Rule
rules.body: Whatever goes wrong is told in one place: the status button and its «Что не так». A part of the page never carries its own error panel, banner or retry button; it keeps its shape and points to the one place. Reasons, actions and SoundCloud's answer live there, one click away.

rules.name: The Useful Retry Rule
rules.body: «Повторить» appears only when asking again can help: not while offline (the app asks by itself when the network returns), not while SoundCloud has said how long to wait (the countdown says when it will ask by itself), never for a part that broke (that is «Перезапустить»). The words agree with the part that failed («История не загрузилась», «Плейлисты не загрузились»).

rules.name: The Kept Shape Rule
rules.body: A part that failed is never replaced by a message: it keeps its size and skeleton at 45 % so the page does not jump, and fills in where it stands when it comes back. One broken part never takes the page down.

rules.name: The Own Order Rule
rules.body: A part plays again as it was heard: oldest first, from the row pressed (or the first) onward, skipping only what can no longer play; the player names it («Из дневника · ночь на 4-е»), and what plays is written down again.

rules.name: The Honest Ending Rule
rules.body: A play says how it ended, in words and as a bar of how far it got. Only the play the player is on reads live; an open play the player is not on (the window closed or reloaded mid-song) reads as stopped where it stopped, which is how it will be written.

rules.name: The Said Where Rule
rules.body: The diary says where it is kept and what its light is reckoned from: «Только на этом компьютере» stands on the light, and a place guessed from the time zone says «· по часовому поясу» until a city is named.

dos: **Do** take every accent from `--glow-1`/`--glow-2`/`--glow-3`; let a cover change the whole window.
**Do** keep the ground near-black (`#08080a`) and separate surfaces by tonal steps (ground, dock, panel, panel-hover).
**Do** make the primary action a white pill with ink text, and give secondary actions on the light the smoky fill with a 1 px inner rim.
**Do** set the one big word in Unbounded 800 scaled to its container, and everything else in Manrope at 600 or heavier.
**Do** show real artwork wherever a track, playlist or person appears, with the quiet tile fallback.
**Do** put grain over any surface that shows the light, and fade the light's edges.
**Do** stop or slow every running animation when the window is hidden, off screen, paused or under reduced motion.

**Do** say in the interface why something does not work (region, Go+ preview, offline, expired sign-in), on the row or tile and before play: unplayable covers are dimmed and disabled with the reason as their second line; Go+ previews carry their chip.
**Do** let a page's own light take the colours of what is pointed at or opened, and give it back when the pointer leaves.
**Do** window any list that can run into thousands, and keep the actions row in reach while it scrolls.
**Do** lead a search with its answer: the artist it names, by the strict test of The Answer First Rule, else the query and its tracks; show found tracks as rows, so a long title can be read.
**Do** offer only filter choices the results hold, with their counts.
**Do** read hotkeys by physical key and keep them quiet while typing; name each control's key in its title.
**Do** say what really happened and what will happen: «Уже играло» only for what played, and how the queue ends where it ends.
**Do** gather everything that went wrong in the status button and «Что не так», and show the button only while something is wrong.
**Do** keep a failed or broken part's shape as its skeleton at 45 % with one smoke pill, and grey the light while there is no network or sign-in.
**Do** say how each play ended («дослушал», «пропустил на 0:12») with a bar of how far it got, and play a part again in its own order.
**Do** let the selection explain itself only from what the diary holds now: why this track, why a source is empty and when it fills, how much is learned, «правила по умолчанию» before anything is.
donts: **Don't** add a fixed brand accent, SoundCloud's orange as a UI colour, or Yandex Music's signature yellow; a mood turn must never produce yellow.

**Don't** put borders around cards or tiles; `line` belongs only to the player bar's top edge, floating menus (and the rules inside them), the sheets over the player and the rule under a list's column heads.
**Don't** put veil wells on the light; there they are smoke with a rim.
**Don't** hide a track's name until hover; the caption under a cover is always there.
**Don't** set track titles, buttons or sentences in Unbounded, or use Manrope below 600.
**Don't** use stroked outline-only or square-cornered buttons; actions are filled pills and circles, or bare muted icons and text.
**Don't** let colour transitions jump or the light run at full frame rate while idle.
**Don't** add eyebrow labels or kickers above titles; a section is named by its title alone.
**Don't** take a Cmd or Ctrl shortcut for a hotkey, or let a single-key hotkey fire while someone types.
**Don't** put an error panel, banner or retry button in place of a part that failed, or offer «Повторить» where asking again cannot help.
